blocks.text: Española: Punta Suárez and Gardner Bay

provenance.rationale: Compose the existing day title from the three place names in the approved Word day-17 paragraph.

blocks.text:
Española: at Punta Suárez, blue-footed and Nazca boobies, mockingbirds and, from about April to December, waved albatrosses, which breed almost only here, with a cliff-top “runway” and a spectacular blowhole; in the afternoon, the white-sand beach of Gardner Bay with its sea lions. (B, L, D)

The morning trail follows an open, rocky volcanic shore with little tall vegetation, making the birds easy to see. You may also see red-billed tropicbirds, Galápagos hawks and lava lizards, with the sound of the ocean along the island's edge.

Almost all 12,000 pairs of Galápagos waved albatrosses breed here. The birds use air currents and the slope of the high cliff to take off. Colonies of boobies and other seabirds line the route, and seawater is forced upwards through the blowhole.

The morning walk is about 3 km, with a dry landing and a difficult level of walking.

After lunch, the yacht approaches Gardner Bay. Sea lions lie right on its long white-sand beach. You can walk along the shore or enter the water. While snorkelling, you may encounter colourful fish and young sea lions, which often approach people out of curiosity; on land, you may see mockingbirds.

Activities include snorkelling, a motorboat ride, kayaking and a short walk of about 1 km. The landing is wet and the difficulty level is easy.

Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner.

blocks.text: Santa Cruz – Los Gemelos – mainland Ecuador

provenance.rationale: Compose the existing final-day route from the Word island, twin-crater site and return to Quito or Guayaquil.

blocks.text:
Santa Cruz: Los Gemelos, twin craters formed by the collapse of the ground into empty lava chambers; transfer to Baltra for your flight to Quito or Guayaquil and your international connection. (B)

In the morning, visit the twin craters on Santa Cruz, on either side of the road between Puerto Ayora and Baltra. Despite their name, these are not volcanic craters: the depressions formed when surface material collapsed into underground cavities and fissures.

The walk is easy, with a dry landing. After visiting the information centre, transfer to Baltra Airport and fly to the mainland.

On arrival in Quito or Guayaquil, make your own way to the international terminal and check in for your onward flight.

By this point, the journey has taken you through 3 very different natural worlds in Ecuador. In the Amazon, you have seen lowland rainforest from the water and from canopy level; in the Andes, high-altitude páramo, volcanoes and cloud forest; and in the Galápagos, an island ecosystem where wildlife takes centre stage. The final flight to the mainland completes the programme without an additional overnight stay. The style of travel has changed several times along the way: private mainland excursions, group programmes in reserves, an Amazon lodge stay and a cruise. These different experiences reveal several sides of the country while following a continuous route.

Meals: breakfast.
